sections.What we use it for:
`kac.tests` asserts what `kac.core` does with a corpus it builds for the purpose. `kac.features` runs Gherkin feature documents through the same runner, so one `dotnet test` command covers either project.

Both projects reference xUnit as `xunit.v3.mtp-off`, beside `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` and `xunit.runner.visualstudio`. The SDK and the runner are what make `dotnet test` find and run the tests, and neither was chosen on its own. The `mtp-off` package keeps `dotnet test` on VSTest. The plain `xunit.v3` package makes each project a Microsoft.Testing.Platform app, and the .NET 10 SDK refuses to run one of those under VSTest.

The third layer, `tooling/kac-tests.cs`, uses none of this. It is a file-based program. It compares `kac` output against committed goldens, and reports its own results.
